text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All newspapers lead with Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob being named new domestic trade and consumer affairs minister, replacing Abu Hassan Omar, who was named chief minister designate of Selangor state.
-- Detention under the proposed amendments to the Internal Security Act can be as short as six months or longer than the existing two years.

-- Expressing concern over damage to underground electricity cables, acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim warned contractors carrying out digging works that they risk facing suspension apart from heavier fines.

-- United Engineers (M) Bhd, which expects to submit a proposal to upgrade and expand the North-South Expressway to the government by the end of the year, does not rule out the possibility of a toll hike or a longer concession period to help recover the cost of the exercise.
-- Lankhorst (M) Bhd, a leading construction and engineering group, has obtained approval from the Securities Commission to be listed on the KLSE Second Board.
-- Malaysia Airlines' 50 billion yen issue will be used for working capital and to partly finance the airline's acquisition of new aircraft for fleet modernisation.
-- The MBf Group has decided to establish its card-processing centre in the Multimedia Super Corridor and plans to eventually offer the processing services to other companies.
